questions.stem: To estimate the gradient of a curve at a point, you should:

options.text: Draw a chord between two far-apart points
Draw a tangent line at that point
Find the area under the curve

questions.explanation: The gradient of a curve at a point is found by drawing a tangent (a straight line that just touches the curve at that point) and finding the gradient of that tangent line.

questions.stem: A tangent to a curve at point P passes through (1, 3) and (5, 11). What is the gradient of the curve at P?
questions.explanation: Gradient of tangent = (11 - 3)/(5 - 1) = 8/4 = 2. The gradient of the curve at P equals the gradient of the tangent at P.

questions.stem: At a turning point of a curve, the gradient is:
questions.explanation: At a turning point (maximum or minimum), the tangent line is horizontal, so the gradient is 0.

questions.stem: On a distance-time curve, the gradient at a specific time gives:

options.text: The instantaneous speed at that time

questions.explanation: The gradient of a distance-time graph at a point gives the instantaneous speed at that moment. A chord gives the average speed.

questions.stem: If the gradient of a curve is positive and increasing, the curve is:
questions.explanation: Positive gradient means the curve is going up. Increasing gradient means it is getting steeper.
